rounds.proof_sketch: With size=128 and block_size=256, thread 255 has idx=255 >= size, so thread_loss=0.0f always. The OOB write to shared_mem[255] is always 0.0f. Thread 127's OOB read at shared_mem[255] either reads the written 0.0f (if hardware allows OOB) or garbage. Since input values don't control thread 255's computation (it's beyond data range) or the OOB memory content, no value pattern can expose a difference.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation causes out-of-bounds shared memory accesses at index 255 (both write by thread 255 and read by thread 127 during reduction). However, thread 255's contribution is always 0.0f because its global index (255) exceeds the data size (128), making the OOB write value constant regardless of input values. The OOB memory region is not addressable through input tensor values. The 112 test rounds showed consistent correct results, indicating the hardware handles these OOB accesses in a way that happens to produce correct results. Since we can only vary input values (not shapes), and the OOB behavior is shape-determined, we cannot craft inputs that expose different behavior.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The OOB access pattern depends on shape (128 elements with 256 threads), not values. To kill it, one would need either: (1) a shape where thread 255 computes non-zero loss (size >= 256), or (2) ability to corrupt OOB memory through other means - neither is possible under the testing constraints.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for CUDA kernels should include shape variations when the mutation affects memory layout or access patterns. This OOB bug would be clearly exposed with input size >= 256 where thread 255 has valid non-zero data. Static analysis tools should flag shared memory sizes that don't match block dimensions.
